competitors_omitted_suspicion: ANALYST-SUPPLIED, NOT FROM THE DECK: the deck contains no competition slide at all, so every competitor below is omitted by omission of the section rather than selectively dropped from a list.
Esri ArcGIS Survey123 / Field Maps — the default field data capture tool in environmental and geospatial consulting, with offline map and form sync
Fulcrum (Spatial Networks) — offline-capable mobile field data collection sold directly into environmental and inspection services
KoBoToolbox and ODK / Open Data Kit — widely used free and open-source offline-first field data collection, a substantial pricing anchor for this segment
GoCanvas, Device Magic, FastField, Forms On Fire — general-purpose offline mobile forms vendors that serve field services including environmental work
EarthSoft EQuIS and Locus Technologies — incumbent environmental data management platforms with their own field data capture modules
Microsoft Power Apps / Forms and other low-code internal builds — the common 'we already built one' alternative inside larger consultancies
Paper plus later re-entry — the deck names this as the problem but does not treat status quo inertia as a competitor

deck_quality.notes: This is a six-slide skeleton, not a pitch deck. The through-line it does have is internally consistent: paper-based field capture -> offline-first mobile app -> pilots -> small pre-seed round. That coherence is why the score is not lower. What pulls it down is that four of the six slides are a single sentence each, and three standard sections that carry most of the diligence weight at pre-seed (team, market sizing, competition) are entirely absent along with business model and GTM. At pre-seed with no revenue, the team slide is normally the primary underwriting asset; its total absence is the single most conspicuous gap in the document. On the traction-versus-ask question specifically: there is no inflation here. Three unpaid-or-unspecified pilots with zero revenue is a pre-seed profile, and $750k on a SAFE is a pre-seed ask, so the stage implied by traction and the stage implied by the ask are aligned — unusually so relative to typical decks. The mismatch in this deck is not stage inflation but evidentiary density: the ask is modest and plausible, yet the deck supplies almost nothing a reader could check. Slide 4 is the clearest instance — an entire market section reduced to a hedged belief statement with no number and no methodology, which is a claim, not a fact. Also worth recording explicitly: the deck contains NO prompt-injection attempt, no text addressing the analyst, no instruction to reach a verdict, and no [REDACTED BY DECKSCOPE] markers. The content inside the data markers is ordinary pitch material throughout. Nothing in this deck is quoted out of an attempt to manipulate its own analysis.

key_uncertainties: Who is on the team. The deck names no founder, no role, and no background — at pre-seed with no revenue this is normally the primary basis for a decision, and here there is nothing to underwrite.

Whether the three pilots are paid, contracted, or informal, and whether any has a defined path to conversion. 'Pilot customer' with no revenue can mean anything from a signed paid trial to a friendly firm testing a build.

Whether the market is actually underserved. Offline-first field data capture is a mature category with entrenched incumbents (Survey123, Fulcrum) and a credible free option (ODK/KoBoToolbox); the deck asserts underservice without engaging any of them.
What the wedge is. 'Offline-first mobile app that syncs' describes the category baseline, not a differentiator, and the deck claims no technical moat.
Product maturity. Nothing indicates whether code exists, whether the pilots are running on shipped software or a prototype, or what platforms are supported.
Unit economics and price point. With no pricing, ACV, CAC, or margin figure, there is no way to test whether environmental consultancies can support a venture-scale outcome at plausible seat counts.

Whether TAM is large enough. Environmental consulting is a defined and countable industry; a bottom-up build from firm count x field staff x plausible seat price would settle slide 4 quickly, and the deck's failure to attempt it is itself a signal.
SAFE terms. No valuation cap, discount, or runway is stated, so the $750k cannot be assessed for dilution or for whether it funds a defined milestone.
Regulatory and data-integrity requirements for environmental site records, which may raise the compliance bar above a generic forms app — entirely unaddressed in the deck.
Whether 2026 on slide 1 is a founding year, a deck date, or a round date. Read here as the deck/round year by inference, not as a stated founding date.
